audit_findings.title: Growth may be unfunded if expansion capex was excluded from owner earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Excluding growth-related store, distribution and IT investment from OE while applying positive growth overstates distributable OE and its terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate that we will spend approximately $875 million, net of approximately $55 million of landlord allowances, in capital expenditures during Fiscal 2026, including approximately $420 million, net of the previously mentioned landlord allowances, for store expenditures (new stores, downsizes, remodels and other store expenditures).
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated anchor error because the maintenance-versus-expansion classification was not supplied. It is nevertheless material: filed FY2026 net capital spending is $875 million, versus the $315.3 million OE anchor, and the latest filing assigns $445 million to stores and $290 million to supply chain. Even a modest recurring portion omitted from OE could materially reduce the 3%-5% growth cases.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $315.3 million anchor to operating cash flow and all capital expenditures, classify each store, supply-chain and IT category, then rerun every scenario using OE after the reinvestment required for its growth rate.

audit_findings.title: The full cash add-back may not be surplus or distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $703.686 million ($10.62 per share; 13.7% of base equity value)
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash that is restricted, needed for seasonal working capital, committed capital spending or debt settlement should not be added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Parent Company’s ability to pay dividends on Parent Company’s common stock will be limited by restrictions on the ability of Parent Company's subsidiaries to pay dividends or make distributions under the terms of current and future agreements governing the indebtedness of Parent Company’s subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate holding-company restrictions and substantial cash needs, but do not establish how much of the $703.686 million is unavailable. The entire add-back represents $10.62 per share; removing it would reduce base value from $77.49 to about $66.87 and the base buy-below level from $54.24 to about $46.81. That would not close the gap to the $265.33 market price, but it is material to the stated intrinsic value and entry price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain cash balances by legal entity, restricted-payment capacity, covenant calculations, minimum seasonal liquidity, committed capital spending and convertible-settlement requirements; rerun the bridge with only demonstrably excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Uncommenced leases are omitted claims whose cost is absent from historical OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Future rent, occupancy, pre-opening and working-capital costs could reduce forecast OE, while the associated new-store earnings could increase it.
audit_findings.evidence: The above schedule excludes approximately $536.9 million for 96 stores and one office the Company has committed to open, expand or relocate but has not yet taken possession of the space.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing discloses $610.5 million of nominal commitments for 99 stores and additional office space that are outside recorded lease liabilities. This is not a demonstrated valuation error because gross lease payments should not simply be deducted from an equity OE bridge, and the locations should also generate earnings. The record does not show whether the scenario growth rates include both sides or establish the net present-value effect.
audit_findings.action: Build a location-level forecast of rent, occupancy, pre-opening costs, working capital and incremental earnings for the committed sites, then rerun OE growth using only the net contribution.

audit_findings.title: Convertible-note dilution does not match the debt treatment in the numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: 0.903561 million shares; at most approximately $1.08 per base-case share
audit_findings.mechanism: The gross conversion shares enlarge the denominator even though principal must be settled in cash and only conversion value above principal can be share-settled.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will pay cash for the aggregate principal amount of 2027 Convertible Notes being converted, and pay (and deliver, if applicable) cash, shares of the Company’s common stock or a combination thereof, at its election, in respect of the remainder (if any) of the Company’s conversion obligation in excess of such aggregate principal amount.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual mismatch is demonstrated. The remaining $186.071 million principal multiplied by the 4.8560 conversion rate produces the included 0.903561 million shares, or 1.36% of the 66.245928 million-share denominator. Even removing all those shares would increase base value only from $77.49 to about $78.57, still far below $265.33; a proper excess-value-share calculation would have a smaller effect.
audit_findings.action: Rerun the denominator using only excess-value shares under the chosen settlement assumption, with consistent adjustments for the $186.071 million principal, cash settlement and retained interest expense.

audit_findings.title: A disclosed one-time gain may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $12.716 million pretax; approximately $2.70 per base-case share before tax adjustment
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring gain left in the OE anchor is treated as recurring and capitalized through the explicit forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The improvement in other income was primarily driven by a one-time settlement of certain layaway liabilities, resulting in a gain.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the $315.3 million anchor is unresolved. The full $12.716 million equals 4.0% of the anchor; conservatively scaling base operating value before tax effects gives an impact of about $178.6 million, or $2.70 per share. That would lower base value only to about $74.79 and cannot change the valuation conclusion. Consistent treatment of the $11.657 million security-tag write-off would reduce the net distortion further unless that write-off was separately added back.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the normalization ledger, remove the layaway gain and security-tag write-off consistently with their tax effects, and confirm the resulting anchor and scenario values.

audit_findings.title: The single-year anchor is exposed to subjective inventory markdown timing
audit_findings.mechanism: Markdown timing changes inventory valuation, gross profit and working-capital conversion in the single period used as OE, potentially raising or lowering the anchor and all capitalized values.
audit_findings.evidence: The judgments involved in determining when to record markdowns can significantly impact the ending inventory valuation and the resulting gross profit.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes estimation sensitivity and identifies markdown timing as a critical audit matter, but it does not demonstrate an error. The disclosed unit sensitivity is $2.8 million at cost for a 1% change in retail markdown dollars—about 0.9% of the $315.3 million anchor and approximately $0.59 per base-case share before tax—but it does not bound the plausible timing variance. Materiality therefore cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Compare post-period markdowns, inventory aging, reserves, shrink adjustments and normalized merchandise margins with year-end assumptions; rerun the valuation using a normalized multi-period OE anchor if a timing distortion is identified.
